$comment: Pinch's capability inventory. Every entry claims evidence — a file or symbol a reader can open. scripts/market.js refuses to credit a capability it cannot prove, and refuses to propose one marked out-of-scope however unanimous the market is. Update this file when a capability lands or dies; a stale inventory makes every comparison wrong in the flattering direction.
$policy: in-scope may be proposed. settled has been decided and is only shown so the decision stays visible. out-of-scope contradicts the product identity in .github/prompts/self-improvement.md; the researcher reports it and the proposer is forbidden from acting on it.

capabilities.name: Runs a local model with no cloud account
evidence: src/brain.js: ollama provider is the default
capabilities.note: The identity of the product. Everything else is optional on top.

capabilities.name: Optional cloud model when the user configures one
evidence: src/brain.js: openai-compatible provider via OPENAI_API_KEY

capabilities.name: Switch between models without editing a file
evidence: src/config.js: LLM_PROVIDER and OLLAMA_MODEL are read from .env at boot
capabilities.note: Changing model means editing .env and restarting. Every comparable product has a picker.

capabilities.name: Streams the reply as it is generated
evidence: src/brain.js: streamLines handles both provider envelopes

capabilities.name: Executes commands and edits files, with approval
evidence: src/tools.js: shell, read_file, write_file, list_dir, grep
src/server.js: approval gate

capabilities.name: Reachable from the chat apps a person already uses
evidence: src/channels/telegram.js
src/channels/discord.js
src/channels/slack.js
src/channels/whatsapp.js
src/channels/ws.js

capabilities.name: Talk to it and have it read replies back
evidence: src/server.js: WHISPER_URL for incoming audio
capabilities.note: Input works with a configured whisper endpoint. Replies are not spoken back, and nothing is offline out of the box.

capabilities.name: Remembers facts between conversations
evidence: src/tools.js: remember, recall, forget
src/store.js: memory.json

capabilities.name: Schedules things and reminds you
evidence: src/scheduler.js
src/tools.js: remind, list_reminders, cancel_reminder
src/timeparse.js

capabilities.name: Looks things up on the web
evidence: src/tools.js: search_web

capabilities.name: Shows where an answer came from
evidence: src/sources.js: a per-turn registry — only what this turn actually retrieved can be cited
src/citations.js: citedIds() / validateCitations() — [1], [1,3] and [1-3], checked against the registry
src/guard.js: 'invented-citation' — a [n] with no source behind it is reported to the user
test/citations.test.js: 'the guard flags a citation to something this turn never fetched'
docs/GUIDE.md: the 'Where the answer came from' section
capabilities.note: Validated, not decorative. Every citation is checked against the list of things the turn actually fetched, and a citation that names nothing becomes a visible guard flag rather than a dead link. Sources come from web search, files read, and attachments — not from the model's memory. What this does NOT do: verify that a source supports the sentence it is attached to. That is a semantic judgement, and a code-level check that claims to make it would be lying.

capabilities.name: Accepts screenshots, documents and files
evidence: src/attachments.js: PDF (FlateDecode), DOCX (zip), UTF-8 text, image passthrough
src/server.js: POST /api/attach
public/index.html: attach button, drag-and-drop, clipboard paste
test/attachment-http.test.js: proves the text reaches the model
capabilities.note: Text, PDF, DOCX and images. No OCR for scanned PDFs, no .doc/.xls, nothing written to disk — attachments live in memory for one message.

capabilities.name: Understands images with a vision model
evidence: src/brain.js: text-only message shape

capabilities.name: Indexes your documents and answers from them
evidence: search_web is network-only; there is no embedding store

capabilities.name: Plugs into MCP servers for third-party tools
evidence: src/mcp.js: JSON-RPC over stdio, initialize → tools/list → tools/call
src/tools.js: registerTool() — dynamic registry, refuses to shadow a built-in
test/mcp.test.js: 'a third-party tool is offered to the model over HTTP'
docs/GUIDE.md: the PINCH_MCP section
capabilities.note: stdio transport only, and every tool from an untrusted server goes through the approval gate. No HTTP/SSE transport, no server-side resources or prompts, no OAuth.

capabilities.name: A documented way to add tools without editing core files
evidence: src/tools.js: tools are a fixed list in this file
docs/GUIDE.md: 'adding a tool' section
capabilities.note: Adding a tool means editing src/tools.js. Fine for one maintainer, a wall for anybody else.

capabilities.name: An agent that runs a task on a schedule without you
evidence: src/schedules.js: parseCadence() accepts `every 30m`, `daily at 09:00`, `weekly on mon at 8:00` — nothing else parses
src/scheduler.js: runSchedules() — a due schedule is a full agent turn, delivered back to the chat that created it
src/agent.js: runAgent({autonomy:'unattended'}) refuses every dangerous tool before the approval gate
test/schedules.test.js: 'an unattended turn refuses a dangerous tool and leaves no approval pending'
docs/GUIDE.md: the 'Tasks that run without you' section
capabilities.note: No catch-up: a schedule missed while the machine was asleep runs once, late, not N times. Interval cadences are measured from the last run, daily/weekly resolve in the owner's timezone, minimum interval 5 minutes, at most 20 schedules. An unattended turn can never approve anything — dangerous tools are refused and the refusal is in the transcript — and it cannot create further schedules, so a loop cannot spawn loops. PINCH_SCHEDULED_RUNS=0 stops all of it.

capabilities.name: Searches everything you have ever said to it
evidence: src/store.js: sessions are listed and loaded by id, never searched

capabilities.name: Exports your conversations and data
evidence: data/ is plain JSON on disk, so a user can copy it — but nothing in the product exports it
capabilities.note: The files are readable with cat by design, which is not the same as a supported export.

capabilities.name: Saved prompts and personas you can reuse
evidence: src/prompt.js: one persona assembled at boot from OWNER_NAME and PINCH_PROFILE

capabilities.name: Customisable interface
evidence: public/index.html: a single hard-coded lobster palette
capabilities.note: The lobster theme is a product requirement, not a limitation. Light/dark is a separate question.

capabilities.name: A native phone app
evidence: public/index.html is installable as a PWA
scripts/pair.js prints a QR
capabilities.note: A PWA that installs from the browser. Cheaper than an app and enough for one person.

capabilities.name: Separate accounts and permissions for several people
evidence: PINCH_KEY is one shared secret; there is no user table
capabilities.note: Deliberately out of scope: one person, one laptop. Not a gap to close, a boundary to keep.

capabilities.name: A local record of what each turn did
evidence: src/telemetry.js: one NDJSON line per turn, rotated at 5 MB
GET /api/health: p50/p95, error rate, guard-flag rate
test/batch2.test.js: 'a completed turn is recorded, and health reports the numbers'
capabilities.note: Local only, never transmitted, and it records timings and counts — not message text. No dashboards and no distributed tracing: this is a file you can `tail`, not an observability platform.
